newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds rebound but caution remains.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds rebound but caution remains.

text.p: German Bund futures started Wednesday in a better mood after U.S. Treasuries pulled themselves back from the brink overnight on a reassessment of the NAPM report.
But traders said a number of technical hurdles would prevent the June Bund futures from getting too far, with first resistance emerging at around 99.70.
By 0732 GMT, the DTB June Bund was trading 15 basis points higher on the day at 99.62. The contract nipped through 99.70 to an early high at 99.71, but failed to sustain the upward momentum.
"Treasuries held up quite well overnight and we saw some buyers coming into the (German) market around the 6.00 percent yield level in 10-year cash," said one Franfurt trader.
But he said those buyers were mainly smaller instutions and trading volumes remained thin.

Data released earlier showing Germany's January current account deficit at 9.3 billion marks and its trade surplus at 4.6 billion marks did little to excite the market, traders said, with the main focus still firmly fixed on the U.S..
"Things seem to be stabilising a bit here -- until the next U.S. number," the trader said.
U.S. factory orders data are due at 1500 GMT, with analysts forecasting a 0.9 percent gain in February versus a 2.5 rise in January.
If the numbers spook U.S. Treasuries, Bunds are likely to take a hit too, traders said, but should find support in the 99.25 to 99.30 region.

A Bunds saleswoman also noted buyers keen to get back into the futures market at around the 99.30 to 99.35 level on the June contract, which corresponds to 6.00 percent 10-year cash yields. The benchmark 10-year Bund was yielding 5.974 percent at 100.12 by 0904 GMT.
If the U.S. numbers are relatively friendly, some dealers said a relief rally could push the June Bund as far as 99.90.
But others said this was a little ambitious, instead looking for the contract to close a gap between 99.70 and 99.79 left from last week's close.
